what_was_done: Approval now rests on an allow-list of the raw command text first, with HD8's parsed shape as the second gate: caller.is_vsdd_call requires both. The grammar is one compiled regular expression used with fullmatch on the whole text — optional leading and trailing spaces or tabs; the program, vsdd or a path of safe characters ending in /vsdd; then zero or more arguments, each introduced by one or more spaces or tabs, where an argument is a bare word of safe characters that does not start with = (safe: ASCII letters, digits and _ @ % + = : , . / -; a tilde starts nothing, ~ is not safe), or a bare-word prefix that is empty or ends with = followed by one single-quoted string, or one single-quoted string alone (no single quote, nothing below U+0020 or U+007F inside, followed by a space, a tab or the end of the text). A comment at the pattern says why each excluded character is excluded (double quote, dollar, backtick, backslash, ; & |, < >, parentheses, braces, brackets, * ?, ~, #, !, newline, carriage return) and that the parser's 'not opaque' is never by itself a reason to approve. Any text that fails passes unmarked and undecided, as HD8 says. Tests: an accepted table (bare flags and ids, -C with a path, --name='two words', a single-quoted path with blanks and non-ASCII letters, leading/trailing blanks and tabs); a refused table with one case per excluded character plus the grammar's edges (= starting a word, unterminated quote, 'a'b glue, empty text, wrong program, leading assignment); every bypass command recorded in the ledger for this unit keyed by its finding id; a runner test that sends nine refused forms through the gate as an agent and asserts exit 0, empty stdout (no permissionDecision, no updatedInput) and no marker file; and a seeded property test that drops 200 random junk strings built only from the excluded characters around a valid call and asserts none is approved. Proof: stripping the allow-list from is_vsdd_call in a scratch copy fails the excluded-character, runner and property tests. Confirmation under sh, bash, dash and zsh with canary programs: every adversarial text that passes the grammar ran only the vsdd canary ('$(id)' inside single quotes is literal, as quoted metacharacters are), while the recorded bypass forms ran the hidden command under 11 shell/text pairs — the grammar refuses exactly those. The grammar is stated once in the design, in rewrite/spec/topics/caller-identity.md ('What a plain vsdd call is'), and rule-model.md links there from the updatedInput paragraph; spec_lint reports 0 problems.

In _read_word's double-quote branch, a ${ now takes the plain-text rule: _parameter_plain runs on the text up to the first '}', and when there is no closing brace, or the inner text is not plain (a nested quote, a backslash, a parenthesis, an @ or ! operator), the word counts a substitution. The finding's forms all parse opaque now: the nested-quote forms 'vsdd survey "${x:-"'"}"$(id)''' and 'vsdd survey "${x:-'"'}"$(id)"}', the zsh nest 'vsdd survey "${(e):-\$(id)}"' and the double-quoted setter 'vsdd survey "${x:=\$(id)}${x@P}"' (and the setter feeding ${!x} or $((x))), which through the runner had got the marker, 'allow' and updatedInput. 'vsdd survey "${x:-a b}"' stays judgeable inside quotes. Proof: removing the branch in a scratch copy fails test_parameter_span_inside_double_quotes_counts_substitutions and, with the parser reverted, the runner refusals fall back to the allow-list alone (the ORCH-2 runner test still passes: the two layers hold independently).

The double-quote branch of _read_word now counts a '$[' as a substitution, as the unquoted branch already does, so an escaped \$ inside the span hides nothing: 'vsdd survey "$[a[\$(id)]]"' parses opaque instead of one plain vsdd segment that runs id under sh and bash via the doubly-expanded array subscript. Added to test_brackets_split_or_are_opaque, and the form is among the runner-as-agent refusals. Proof: deleting the branch in a scratch copy fails that test.

A dollar sign followed by a single quote, outside double quotes, now counts a substitution in _read_word's bare branch, because bash and zsh read $'...' as ANSI-C quoting where \' does not end the string while dash reads the POSIX way — the shells disagree on where the string ends, so it is never plain text. Both recorded forms, "vsdd survey $'\'' ; id #'" and "vsdd survey $'\'';id;'x'", parse opaque instead of one plain vsdd call that runs id under sh, bash and zsh. Proof: deleting the branch in a scratch copy fails test_dollar_quote_counts_a_substitution.

Dropped '@' and '!' from _PARAM_PLAIN_CHARS, with the reason at the set: bash 4.4+'s ${name@P} expands the value as a prompt string and runs any $(...) in it (BASH_EXECUTION_STRING holds the command itself under bash -c), and ${!x} is indirect expansion through array subscripts. "vsdd survey '$(id)' ${BASH_EXECUTION_STRING@P}", 'vsdd survey ${x@P}', 'vsdd survey ${!x}' and the double-quoted setters feeding them parse opaque now, where through the runner they had got the marker, 'allow' and updatedInput; ${@} reading opaque is the safe side. Proof: restoring '@!' to the set in a scratch copy fails test_prompt_and_indirect_parameter_operators_count_substitutions.
